pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: src/lib/auth.ts:151 The session the browser carries back is an HMAC-sealed payload under a server-only AUTH_SECRET, checked in constant time with expiry in the payload. The OAuth client secret is attached only server-side, the browser gets only the public Supabase URL and anon key, and upstream OAuth failures reach the browser only as closed error codes.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/auth.ts:151 The session cookie is sealed with HMAC-SHA256 and checked in constant time. decodeSession fails closed with no secret and carries exp/rexp inside the payload.
src/lib/supabase/client.ts:11 Only NEXT_PUBLIC_ values reach the browser client, with a comment saying they are public by design. The secret-bearing auth.ts carries `import "server-only"` at line 9.
src/lib/auth.ts:533 The GitHub client secret is attached server-side during the code exchange. The browser holds only its signed session cookie, and the GitHub token is never persisted to the client.

src/app/api/auth/callback/route.ts:150 The upstream error_description (thrown at auth.ts:543) is logged server-side only, and the browser gets a closed code (oauth_failed/denied/csrf). The Supabase callback does the same at src/app/auth/callback/route.ts:129. No correlation id is returned.

src/lib/supabase/client.ts:3 The browser-held Supabase key is used for auth only here. App data lives in a separate Postgres reached through Prisma, so no aggregate is served to an anonymous role from this context.
src/lib/auth.ts:9 This is a hosted web app holding its own service credentials, not a local app acting with the person's ambient login.
